title: A Millimeter Scale Flexural Testing System for Measuring the Mechanical Properties of Marine Sponge Spicules
protocol: Choose a cantilever with appropriate stiffness for the experiment.
Attach the load point (LP) to the cantilever using #4-40 socket head cap screws (SHCSs).
Ensure not to plastically deform the cantilever arms while attaching the LP.
Wipe the surface of the LP mirror with 2-propanol using a lint-free cotton swab.
Inspect the mirror for scratches and replace if damaged.
Attach the cantilever to the cantilever plate using #6-32 SHCSs with the LPT pointing away from the plate.
Insert 1/8" alignment pins through the cantilever and plate, then tighten the screws and remove the alignment pins.
Retract the FODS by turning the micrometer counter-clockwise as much as possible.
Attach the cantilever plate to the frame loosely using #6-32 SHCSs with the LPT in the specified direction.
Insert 1/8" alignment pins through the frame and cantilever plate, then tighten the screws and remove the alignment pins.
Set the voltage on the power supply to 12.00 V in constant voltage mode using the adjustment knob.
Turn on the voltage output and confirm that the current draw is roughly 60-70 mA on the LCD screen.
Wait at least one hour for the current draw to reach a steady state.
Open and run the Basic_Data program.
Turn the FODS micrometer clockwise until the output voltage displayed on the user interface graph reaches a maximum value.
Adjust the gain of the FODS using the set screws until the voltage output reads 5.0 V.
Turn the FODS micrometer counter-clockwise to retract it fully.
Open the microscope illuminator and adjust the position and focus using the manual translation stages.
Center the LPT in the field of view using the manual translation stages.
Stop the Basic_Data program by clicking the 'Stop' button.
Open the motor controller user interface software.
Move the stage to the maximum travel in the x-axis direction using the potentiometer slider.
Set the home position for the x-axis by clicking the 'Home' button.
Move the stage to the maximum travel in the y-axis direction using the potentiometer slider.
Set the home position for the y-axis by clicking the 'Home' button.
Close the motor controller user interface software.
Seat the stage on the base plate with micrometer heads resting in the divots of the leveling plate.
Place a bubble level on the isolation table and adjust each leg's pressure until the surface is perfectly level.
Move the bubble level to the top of the stage leveling plate.
Adjust the micrometers so that the stage is level.
Note the micrometer positions and remove the stage from the stage base plate.
Run the Basic_Data program and turn the FODS micrometer clockwise until the output voltage is approximately 4 V.
Stop the program by clicking the 'Stop' button.
Measure the mass of the wire hook and calibration weights using an analytical balance.
Open the Cantilever_Calibration program and enter the desired file name for the force calibration output file in the text box in the user interface.
Run the Cantilever_Calibration program and click 'OK' when prompted to enter the mass of the first calibration weight.
Wait for the output voltage displayed in the user interface graph to stop oscillating and click the green 'Voltage Stabilized' button to take a voltage measurement.
Use tweezers to hang the wire hook from the hole in the LPT so that the hook is facing away from the microscope objective.
Use the tweezers to damp the vibration of the cantilever caused by the addition of the hook.
Enter the mass of the hook in grams in the dialog box and click 'OK'.
Wait for the output voltage to stop oscillating before clicking the 'Voltage Stabilized' button.
Use tweezers to hang the first weight on the wire hook and repeat the process of taking a voltage measurement as described in the previous step.
Repeat this step until either all of the calibration weights have been hung or the output voltage is less than 1.8 V.
Click 'Cancel' in the dialog box to exit the Cantilever_Calibration program.
Retract the FODS micrometer counter-clockwise.
Remove the hook and weights from the LPT.
Wear nitrile gloves when handling E. aspergillum sponge skeletons.
Store the skeletons in sealed containers when not being handled.
Use tweezers to grasp one anchor spicule by its distal end.
Pull the spicule to remove it from the skeleton.
Place the spicule on a clean microscope slide.
Hold the spicule against the slide near the midpoint using a #00000 red sable brush.
Cut a ≈4 mm section of the spicule by pushing a razor blade against it perpendicular to the slide surface.
Discard the large distal and proximal sections of the spicule.
Keep the ≈4 mm section.
Inspect the 4-mm spicule section using a polarized light microscope at 10x magnification.
Discard the spicule section and return to step 3.2 if it is missing large regions of silica layers.
Handle inspected spicule sections exclusively using the #00000 red sable brush.
Clean any spicule fragments or other particles from the surface of the sample stage with a brush or compressed air.
Apply a few drops of 2-propanol to a lint free cotton swab and wipe the sample stage.
Avoid contact with the areas of the stage coated with non-reflective paint.
Transfer the spicule section to the sample stage.
Position the spicule section across the trench with the desired span for the bending test.
Gently push the spicule in the direction against the trench ridge.
Ensure that the spicule is perpendicular to the trench edges.
Seat the stage on the stage base plate so that the tips of the micrometer spindles rest in the stage base plate divots.
Adjust the micrometers on the stage leveling plate if needed.
Open the Bending_Test program.
Set the 'step size' to 2 µm.
Set the 'maximum displacement' to 0.5 mm.
Set the 'low voltage stop' to 1.5 V.
Set the 'high voltage stop' to 4.6 V.
Select the desired image directory using the user interface text box.
Select the desired data directory using the user interface text box.
Enter the output file name in the corresponding text box.
Turn off the 'save images' switch in the user interface.
Click the green rectangular button below the words 'Voltage Difference'.
Run the Bending_Test program and wait for motor controller and camera interfaces to initialize.
Turn on the illuminator and adjust brightness so that the LPT is visible.
Adjust the FODS micrometer clockwise until the output voltage displayed is ~1.7 V.
Move the stage in the desired direction using the potentiometer slider until it is ~1 cm below the LPT.
Set the axis home position by clicking the "Home" button.
Position the LPT over the center of the thin steel strip using the potentiometer sliders on the motor controllers.
Move the stage in the X direction until it is within the microscope's field of view.
Monitor the output voltage graph while moving the stage in the Y direction to determine the approximate position where the LPT contacts the surface.
Retract the stage approximately 10 µm when contact is detected.
Enter a value of 0.003 V for 'touch sensitivity' in the user interface.
Enter a value of 0.001 mm for 'touch off step size'.
Click the button labeled "Begin Test".
Wait for the test to complete.
Open and run the Basic_Data program.
Turn the FODS micrometer counter-clockwise until the output voltage displayed on the user interface graph is approximately 3 V.
Use the potentiometer slider on the axis motor controller to position the LPT between the trench edges above the spicule.
Move the stage using the potentiometer slider on the x-axis motor controller until the LPT is below the top surface of the trench ridge.
Bring the front surface of the trench ridge into focus using the potentiometer slider on the y-axis motor controller so that the complete width of the LP is between the edges of the trench ridge.
Stop the Basic_Data program by clicking the 'Stop' button.
Open and run the Center_LoadPoint program.
Move the stage until the LPT is nearly in contact with the right trench edge using the x-axis motor controller.
Click the "Find Edge" button.
Use the x-axis motor controller to move the stage until the LPT is nearly in contact with the left trench edge when prompted.
Click the "Find Edge" button.
Open the Bending_Test program.
Set the step size to 2 µm using the user interface.
Set the maximum displacement to 0.5 mm using the user interface.
Set the low voltage stop to 1.5 V using the user interface.
Set the high voltage stop to 4.5 V using the user interface.
Select the desired image directory using the text boxes in the user interface.
Select the desired data directory using the text boxes in the user interface.
Enter the output file name using the text boxes in the user interface.
Set the 'save images' switch to the up position in the user interface.
Click the green rectangular button below words 'Voltage Difference' so that it is not illuminated.
Run the Bending_Test program and wait for initialization of motor controller and camera interfaces.
Move the stage until the spicule is within the microscope's field of view using the potentiometer slider on the motor controller.
Use the potentiometer slider on the x-axis motor controller to move the stage until the spicule is under the LPT.
Adjust the microscope focus knobs so that the spicule is in focus in the user interface.
Turn the FODS micrometer counter-clockwise until the output voltage is approximately 1.8 V.
Use the potentiometer slider on the z-axis motor controller to move the stage while watching the output voltage graph in the user interface.
Determine the approximate position at which the LPT contacts the spicule by looking for a change in voltage with further movement of the stage.
Retract the stage approximately 50 µm.
Click "Begin Test".
Wait until the bending test is completed.
Note that the stage will move in 2 µm increments in the specified direction, bending the spicule.
Observe the FODS output voltage for stopping conditions: maximum stage displacement of 0.5 mm reached, spicule breaks, or high voltage limit of 4.5 V reached.
Prompt user to end test or override previous value if maximum displacement is reached.
Allow user to increment the stage displacement limit or reverse direction when 'Override' is selected.
Enable user to change the stage displacement step direction by clicking "Reverse Loading" at any point during the test.
Wait for the bending test output file generation, which has a tab-delimited structure similar to the voltage-displacement interpolation output file.
Turn the FODS micrometer counter-clockwise until the FODS is at least 5 mm from the LPT mirror.
Carefully remove the stage from the stage base plate.
